pañca: [Paci+a.(pañcana-saṃ)]  CL=7 The word "pañca" expresses both numerical value (saṅkhyā) and countable objects (saṅkheyya). It is always plural and, being a gender-neutral (aliṅga) term, maintains the same form in all three genders, and does not take feminine suffixes. [Rū. 250, 227. Rū.Ṭī. 227. Nirutti. 251]. The Visuddhārāma Mahārūpasiddhi Nissaya states that the Rūpasiddhi Ṭīkā"s statement (227) about expressing numerical values might be a later addition. The Abhidhāna (1073), Amarakosa (19, 83), and its commentary Mahesvara indicate that number words from "dvi" to "aṭṭhārasa" only express countable objects, not numerical values. [Udāna.Ṭ.385. Nīti.pada.p.100 also refer]. Examples: 5 items, 5 kinds, 5 types, 5 persons (etc.).

[Pa+ñā+a+ā]  CL=9 That which analyzes, discriminates, considers, contemplates and knows in various ways; knowledge, intelligence, understanding, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom cetasika.
Wisdom (pañña) is that which understands. What does it understand? The Noble Truths through the method of 'This is suffering' and so forth. In the Commentary it is said 'pañña is that which makes known.' What does it make known? It makes known 'impermanence, suffering, and non-self.' Abhi.Ttha.1.165. Wisdom is that by which a person understands, or that which understands by itself. Suttani.Ttha.1.131. Mind, intelligence, wisdom, understanding, knowledge, reason, and insight. Dhan.152. Wisdom is that by which things are known. Dhan.Ti.152. [References to various commentaries follow].
